If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. 132	## 4. Spec problems (with passage and example)
133	
134	**P1. `HandlePool` and `DataStack` contracts are outside `specs/`, yet the brief requires their verdicts.** §75: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here." AGENTS.md: "`specs/` is normative and the only source of semantics." Spec v0 constrains them only through §36 (`MetaRight`), §56 (guard), §37 and §89 ("a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure"), §9. Examples with no deciding clause: H31b (`resolveMany Modify` with two handles on one entry → `fail` or `reject`?); `pool_free_entry_handle` H3:977 (`freeSlot` of a free slot at its current generation: v0.4 D.3 only says it "n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité"); `case_aba` DS:927 (`rewind` of a removed mark → `fail`); `freeSlot` with a derived `internal` (v0.4 D.3 vs §69.2 literal). These verdicts cannot be fixed from the spec.
135	
136	**P2. MM23-H15/H16 expected verdicts rest on jalon-2 decisions 2 and 3, which spec v0 does not contain.** §82.3: "an authority `store` must correspond to writing an actual reference into a single logical leaf with an appropriate representation"; §81 leaves "representation criteria and typed formation of accesses (Spec 4); … encodings (Spec 11)" undetermined. Example: run R6 (H23:745) `issue [5, 4]` into 2, leaf 4 at offset 0, leaf 5 at offset 8: writing address base+8 (head) or base (lowest) both satisfy §82 as written. The brief says H15/H16 "must now pass"; that requires a recorded decision (spec text or DESIGN.md parameter of the refinement relation), not a silent choice.
137	
138	**P3. MM23-H09: deallocation of automatic storage at `exitFrame` is not specified.** §9: "The kernel also represents storage with static or automatic duration, whose particular rules will be defined later." §73: "Exiting does not entail automatic physical deallocation of all dead places." Example: R1 exit (H23:503) — a realization emitting three `DeallocStep` for locals 0, 1, 2 and one emitting none both satisfy §73 and §82.5; the material expects three.
139	
140	**P4. Byte-copy provenance (MM2-H13a, MM23-H04/H13).** §10: "Rules for propagation of provenance during byte copies and reinterpretations are not yet fixed"; §19: "Undecided: … propagation through representation copies." Against §20.2 (a read "supplies the sequence of abstract bytes actually read, including provenance") and §16 (a write stores "the supplied representation and its provenance information"). Example: `ReadStep` of an 8-byte pointer returns `[init v (some a)]×8`; a `WriteStep` supplying those abstract bytes stores `some a` by §16, but §10 says the copy's propagation is not fixed. H13a "la provenance de chaque octet est conservée" holds at relation level only if the copy supplies the read abstract bytes; at language level it is open.
141	
142	**P5. `transfer` creating an ownership cycle not caught by any listed precondition.** §63 lists no arrival-usability clause; §63.8 checks only `corr(r)`; §58: "An `ok` transition must … preserve the relevant invariants." Example: x (Init) owns y (alloc owner x), y owns z (alloc owner y, leaf, Uninit); `transfer(x, z)`: §63.1–§63.5 hold; §63.6–§63.7 are vacuous for the then-unusable places; §63.8 holds (root of y covers leaves of y, `corr(x) = z` ∉ footprint(y)); effect: y owned by z, z owned by y — an ownership cycle (§40 "An ownership cycle makes no place usable"), active roots of y and z covering unusable places (`NoDangling`, §54). Whether §58 acts as an implicit rejection is not stated. The draft has an explicit clause "`(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst`" (M3:1243) which spec v0 does not list. Concerns H13's class of cases.
143	
144	**P6. Frame ownership of `enterFrame` locals is implicit.** §72.2: "introduction of locals preserves well-formedness and the validity of their roots"; §39: "Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places"; §70.1 speaks of "an ordinary local directly owned by a frame"; §47 explicitly allows a static owned by another static, with no analogue for locals. Example: H27b's draft shape `(none, some 0, 0)` (H3:505), a local root owned by local 0, is not excluded by any §72 clause; it would be an `OwnedRoot` freeable by §70. The brief treats "locals owned by frame" as a spec v0 rule; the text does not state it.
145	
146	**P7 (outside corpus scope, for the kernel mapper).** §36: "Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations" vs §71.2: provider "updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata". Example: provider leaf `SharedMutable`, frame holding only `Observe` on it, `alloc(provider, owner, shape)` passes §71's static preconditions. No corpus case uses it.
147

# ERN — Jalon 3 : matériel pour revue unique

**Objet :** validation adversariale du Memory Model (spec 1) après les jalons 1 et 2.
**Contenu :** les trois corpus mis à jour, le contrat du pool de handles, le cadrage de la décision `NoLock`, le registre des obligations inter-spécifications.
**Statut :** matériel de conception, non normatif. Version 2 : corrections de la revue unique de GPT intégrées (contrat du pool, corpus, calendrier, scénarios Weld).

## 0. Règles du jalon 3

1. **Oracle indépendant.** Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer ».
2. **Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction.
3. **États atteints.** Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés.
4. **Pas de correction silencieuse.** Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause.
5. **Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3.
6. **Couverture.** La colonne « Couvert » indique un témoin déjà produit pendant les jalons 1 et 2, quand il est identifié avec certitude. Le jalon 3 rejoue tous les cas depuis l'état initial, couverts ou non, dans un module de cas séparé.
7. **Cible des corpus.** MM3-H et MM23-H sont encodés au jalon 3 sur les brouillons, sans modifier `MM02`, `MM03` ni `MM23`. MM2-H : ses verdicts sont révisés au jalon 3, mais sa validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence ; le jalon 3 ne le déclare pas validé.
8. **Écarts connus.** Un cas dont le verdict attendu repose sur une décision non encore appliquée au brouillon (MM23-H15, H16) est encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu », et inscrit au registre de reconstruction. Il n'est jamais présenté comme réussi.

---

## 2. Corpus MM2-H — machine abstraite MM-02

## 7. Registre de la reconstruction de référence

0. Exécution de MM2-H (17 cas) contre la reconstruction de MM-02 ; MM23-H15 et H16 rejoués après application des décisions 2 et 3 du jalon 2.
1. Écarts du brouillon MM-03 trouvés au jalon 2 (passe 1, (f) 1–6) : utilisabilité des feuilles lues et écrites ; empreintes faites de feuilles ; une racine par `alloc` ; marques de mort transitives ; `RootLive` ; bonne fondation des chaînes de possession.
2. Locaux d'`enterFrame` possédés directement par le cadre (O6, à écrire dans la v0.3).
3. Décisions 1 à 4 du jalon 2 : disjonction déclarée par feuilles ; pointeur d'une région vide ; adresse la plus basse ; feuille de référence de la taille d'un pointeur.
4. Théorèmes à énoncer : induction « toute feuille `Init` atteinte a été déclarée ou écrite » ; correspondance `Step` ↔ `Reachable`.
5. Noms Lean des textes normatifs déplacés en annexe de correspondance.

736:# Annexe F — Registre de reconstruction de référence (non normatif)
30:Une **feuille** est un emplacement sans enfant structurel. `footprint(p)` contient les feuilles de `p`, et les droits d'accès sur un emplacement sont évalués sur ces feuilles. Les emplacements possédés transitivement par une valeur ne sont pas automatiquement des feuilles de son `footprint`. Une unité logique de MM-03 ne constitue pas automatiquement une allocation supplémentaire de MM-02.
142:L'ordre numérique des identifiants, la précédence du parent sur l'enfant dans une liste et les bornes des identifiants générés peuvent servir **à représenter ou à démontrer** cette bonne formation dans Lean ; ils ne constituent pas des restrictions normatives sur l'identité des emplacements ou des autorités. La préservation de `WF3` par une transition relève des **théorèmes de préservation**, et non d'une clause supplémentaire du prédicat d'état. `WF3` n'impose pas de disposition physique particulière des objets : celle-ci appartient au raffinement vers MM-02.
198:I5, lié au stockage épinglé, reste une **obligation spécialisée** de `K.Pinned`, et non une clause automatiquement déduite des seuls accès séquentiels. Les résultats du jalon 1 démontrent l'invariant ci-dessus **dans le modèle abstrait**, sous les contrats spécifiés ; ils ne prouvent pas encore les correspondances MM-02.
210:`reject` signifie que la discipline statique n'autorise pas le pas ; ce n'est ni un trap runtime implicite, ni un `ub` de MM-02. `fail` est un **échec défini**, laissant l'état inchangé ; seules `alloc` et `issue` peuvent l'émettre dans ce noyau. Pour toutes les autres opérations, l'issue est `ok` ou `reject`. Pour `alloc` et `issue`, le contrôle des préconditions statiques précède la détermination de l'échec dynamique, sauf les précisions d'ordre de contrôle indiquées dans leurs règles.
240:Une déclaration de disjonction non fondée peut invalider la preuve : sans `DDSound`, un `split` accepté peut violer I1. La construction de sous-régions de taille nulle n'est pas identifiée à une allocation de MM-02 ; le cas de la forme vide d'`alloc` est distinct.
317:`Moved` et `Uninit` ne peuvent pas être lus. La définition ne remplace pas les vérifications de représentation et de pointeurs concrets de MM-02.
350:**Effet `ok`** : les feuilles de la valeur `place` deviennent `Uninit` ; `place` **reste utilisable comme emplacement** et pourra être réinitialisé légalement. Les autorités détenues par `place` et par les sous-stockages morts sont libérées ; les dépendances de la valeur terminée sont supprimées ; les emplacements possédés transitivement qui cessent de vivre sont marqués morts. L'opération ne déclenche pas automatiquement une désallocation MM-02 : une allocation non libérée peut constituer une fuite, qui n'est pas interdite par cette garantie. **Autre issue :** `reject`.
361:**Effet `ok`** : `place` et le stockage qui cesse de vivre sont marqués morts ; les autorités de ces régions, y compris les racines correspondantes, deviennent inactives, ainsi que celles dont les détenteurs meurent. Les dépendances survivantes doivent rester valides. La correspondance avec une désallocation MM-02 correcte est une obligation du jalon 2, non un axiome de `free`. **Autre issue :** `reject`.
377:La réussite de l'allocation dépend de l'état du fournisseur : elle ne constitue pas un droit à inventer de la mémoire physique. Le raffinement de cette opération vers `AllocStep` de MM-02 relève du jalon 2.
525:| `Deallocable` | L'emplacement appartient à une unité effectivement libérable | Raccordement à MM-02 au jalon 2 |
526:| `FreeCompat` | L'autorité opaque de désallocation est compatible avec l'unité libérée | Raccordement à MM-02 au jalon 2 |
529:`Invalidates` n'est pas un champ de `K` pour le présent noyau : les conditions structurelles de `reset`, de `free` et des dépendances portent directement les obligations d'invalidation pertinentes. La réalisation de `DDSound` à partir de dispositions mémoire réelles fait partie du raffinement de MM-03 vers MM-02.
531:## 9. Obligations de raffinement vers MM-02
533:MM-03 définit des emplacements logiques, des autorités, des dépendances et leurs transitions. MM-02 définit les allocations, les octets, les emplacements et les opérations mémoire au niveau concret de son propre modèle. **Le jalon 1 n'est pas une preuve de l'implémentation mémoire concrète** : le jalon 2 doit construire une relation de représentation justifiée entre les deux modèles.
537:1. **Emplacements et octets :** associer `P`, les feuilles de `footprint`, leur possession et leurs parties aux unités de stockage, offsets, plages, identités et contraintes d'alignement de MM-02 ; établir une disjonction réelle pour les déclarations `DeclaredDisjoint`.
538:2. **Autorités et opérations :** rattacher les modes effectifs et `ExercisableAt` aux conditions concrètes de lecture, écriture et validité des pointeurs ; montrer qu'un accès sûr MM-03 satisfait les obligations MM-02, sans confondre possession et représentation binaire.
543:7. **Arènes :** relier les entrées d'arènes, les régions, les émissions, le stockage local/statique/alloué et les métadonnées à des opérations MM-02 ; garantir qu'aucune émission ne réintroduit un accès après invalidation.
548:- **R1 — Lecture :** toute lecture sûre autorisée de MM-03 satisfait les préconditions de lecture MM-02.
549:- **R2 — Écriture :** toute écriture sûre autorisée de MM-03 satisfait les préconditions d'écriture MM-02.
553:- **R6 — Raffinement :** chaque effet concret attribué à une transition sûre correspond à une transition autorisée de MM-02.
563:Les preuves portent sur les **accès du noyau abstrait séquentiel**. Elles n'établissent ni l'absence générale de fuites et de blocages, ni la terminaison, ni les propriétés de la concurrence, ni la correction du compilateur ou de la traduction mémoire MM-02. Les garanties différées ne sont pas promises par la présente section.
567:Les cas d'épreuve constituent des témoins de validation d'un modèle ; ils ne donnent pas, par leur seule présence, autorité à des règles qui contrediraient les sections 1–9. Les cas en annexe B reprennent des verdicts effectivement décrits dans les rapports Lean. Les corpus adversariaux complets MM2-H, MM3-H et MM23-H sont **réservés au jalon 3**, sans présumer de verdicts encore absents des sources disponibles.
575:| Raffinement MM-03 → MM-02 (R1, R2, R4, R6), `DDSound` réel, adresses, allocation, désallocation, provenance, épinglage, initialisation, `store` de pointeur, arènes, justification mémoire de `noalias` | **Jalon 2 de la Spec 1** |
577:| Corpus adversariaux MM3-H et MM23-H | **Jalon 3 achevé**, sous les écarts connus explicités dans son rapport ; MM2-H doit encore être exécuté contre la reconstruction de référence. Les cas concurrents dépendants sont à rouvrir après la Spec 2. |
647:**Historique du corpus :** l’inventaire initial comptait `MM2-H` (17), `MM3-H` (43) et `MM23-H` (14). Les corpus MM3-H et MM23-H ont été enrichis et exécutés au jalon 3 (`J3_v0.1.md`). Les verdicts actualisés, les variantes, les cas inter-spécifications et les écarts connus sont consignés dans les annexes du document assemblé. **MM2-H doit être exécuté contre la reconstruction de référence** ; sa présence dans le dossier ne vaut pas preuve de conformité. Les cas concurrents requérant les règles de synchronisation seront alors identifiés comme dépendants de la Spec 2.
679:7. **Écriture d'une valeur et sémantique physique.** `kind` reste non interprété par l'exploration ; `SameShape` est l'isomorphisme ordonné de l'arbre, **pas** une preuve de type, d'alignement, de layout ou d'ABI identiques. La future spécification de types et le raffinement MM-02 devront établir leurs propres obligations. L'initialisation concrète n'est pas déduite d'un simple drapeau logique `Init`.
685:Le registre d'arbitrages A–J reste une **source de traçabilité externe** ; ces identifiants ne sont pas nécessaires au texte normatif final, et aucune ancienne variante contradictoire ne doit subsister après la contre-analyse. La candidate v0.3 ne modifie pas le modèle MM-02 et n'engage pas le jalon 2 avant validation éditoriale.
713:L'effet `ok` applique au **contenu** les effets de fin d'usage d'`endUse`, remet les feuilles de l'entrée à `Uninit`, marque l'entrée libre et incrémente sa génération ; **il ne désalloue pas implicitement l'allocation MM-02 du stockage**. Il ne s'agit pas de supposer une invocation de O12 autorisée par simple `MetaRight` : la correspondance des effets et la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constituent une **obligation explicite de reconstruction**, notamment dans les cas `writeShared`.
746:7. **Corpus MM2-H** : exécuter les 17 identifiants d'origine (H13 scindé en H13a/H13b, donc 18 scénarios) sur la reconstruction de référence, et non sur le vieux brouillon ; conserver les cas de formation d'adresse et reconstruction de pointeur non tranchés par MM-02.G comme obligations, sans les décréter réussis.

# Annexe F — Registre de reconstruction de référence (non normatif)

La reconstruction de référence doit repartir du texte **validé**, et non des approximations du brouillon. Les éléments suivants ne sont pas tous prouvés à ce stade :

1. **Six écarts du brouillon MM-03** (`MM23_v0.1.md`, section (f)) : (i) feuilles lues/écrites utilisables, (ii) empreintes composées uniquement de feuilles, (iii) `alloc` créant une racine unique, (iv) marques de mort transitives après `free` et `endUse`, (v) `RootLive`/`RootHeld`, (vi) bonne fondation des chaînes de possession.
2. **Locaux de `enterFrame`** : rendre explicite que les locaux créés par l'opération sont possédés directement par le cadre ; une forme de local ayant pour propriétaire un autre local n'est pas une forme de `enterFrame` admise.
3. **Jalon 2 — décisions 1 à 4** : (i) disjonction déclarée des **feuilles**, à justifier par la bibliothèque, puis disjonction des plages d'octets sous `LayoutWF` ; (ii) adresse/provenance d'une région vide = base/allocation de son ancre effective ; (iii) pour une région non vide, adresse minimale des feuilles de taille non nulle, sans confondre pointeur et représentation d'une région non contiguë ; (iv) feuille recevant une référence de taille exactement adaptée au pointeur et `decode` lisant uniquement ces octets (obligations Specs 4/11).
4. **Jalon 2 — autres points** : `SameSizeAlong` demeure à la Spec 4, `Repr` inclut `MM02.WF`, `freeSound_derived` et fournisseur conservé, simulation conditionnelle à paramètres fixés ; ne pas présenter le théorème de simulation comme une validation autonome de tous les contenus binaires.
5. **Induction d'initialisation** : toute feuille `Init` atteinte l'était à l'état initial ou provient d'une écriture autorisée, d'un transfert légal ou d'une émission écrivant explicitement sa destination. **Correspondance `Step` / `Reachable`** : démontrer la liaison des constructeurs et transitions opérationnelles générales, non seulement les cas isolés.
6. **Reconstruction `HandlePool`** : réénoncer et prouver `PoolInv` corrigé ; prouver l'effet de `freeSlot` sous `MetaRight`, notamment lorsque seul `writeShared` autorise la mutation des métadonnées ; vérifier `resolveMany Observe`, les deux registres et le stockage `Uninit` de `newPool` ; vérifier la propriété d'exclusivité à travers toutes les opérations du noyau.
7. **Corpus MM2-H** : exécuter les 17 identifiants d'origine (H13 scindé en H13a/H13b, donc 18 scénarios) sur la reconstruction de référence, et non sur le vieux brouillon ; conserver les cas de formation d'adresse et reconstruction de pointeur non tranchés par MM-02.G comme obligations, sans les décréter réussis.
8. **MM23-H15/H16** : enregistrer et corriger les écarts connus de pointeurs vides/ordre des feuilles, sans les présenter comme des preuves déjà acquises.
9. **Option 2 `NoLock`** : reconstruire et vérifier la nouvelle précondition locale de O4 et O18 ; H49 et H51 restent des limites d'ergonomie (cycles d'autorités, non UB) ; l'option 3 globale n'est pas adoptée.
10. **Appels** : enregistrer la primitive de `sink` à l'entrée d'appel et les conditions du ré-emprunt H01 pour la Spec 3, sans les introduire silencieusement dans les transitions courantes de MM-03.

La reconstruction utilisera un journal de traçabilité clause → définition → théorème → cas, et distinguera l'ensemble des garanties effectivement prouvées des conditions de programme bien typé, d'ABI et de bibliothèque.

1	/-!
2	# Elementary memory machine (spec v0, Parts II–III, §8–§20)
3	
4	Source: `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`. Citations: `§N.k` is numbered item `k`
5	of section `N`; `§N ¶p` is the `p`-th paragraph of section `N`, a list belonging to the
6	paragraph that introduces it.
7	
8	* State, allocations, bytes, places and accesses (§9–§12).
9	* Effects of valid operations: `State.write`, `State.dealloc`, `State.alloc`.
10	* Raw operations as transition relations with `ok`/`ub` outcomes, stated on every state
11	  (§20.1): `ReadStep`, `WriteStep`, `DeallocStep`, `AllocStep`. Typed reads and writes carry
12	  a type argument of an opaque type `Ty`; their unspecified obligations are explicit
13	  parameters split into a decidable part `dec` and a static part `stat` (§20.3).
14	* Interpreters `read`, `write`, `dealloc`, `alloc`, computable, with the static part as a
15	  proof argument (§20.3 ¶3), agreeing with the relations in both directions.
16	* Executions `Exec` (sequences of `ok` steps) from any initial state (§9 ¶9).
17	-/
18	
19	namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Machine
20	
21	/-! ## State and accesses (Part II) -/
22	
23	/-- Elementary access authority of a means of access (§12 ¶1, §12 ¶4). -/
24	inductive Auth where
25	  | read
26	  | write
27	  deriving DecidableEq
28	
29	/-- The elementary authority order `read ≤ write`, reflexive (§12 ¶4). -/
30	instance : LE Auth := ⟨fun a b => a = .read ∨ b = .write⟩
31	
32	/-- The elementary authority order is decidable (§12 ¶4). -/
33	instance (a b : Auth) : Decidable (a ≤ b) :=
34	  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (a = .read ∨ b = .write))
35	
36	/-- Abstract byte: uninitialized, or initialized with an 8-bit value and an optional
37	provenance represented by an allocation identity (§10 ¶1–¶3). -/
38	inductive AByte where
39	  | uninit
40	  | init (val : UInt8) (prov : Option Nat)
41	  deriving DecidableEq
42	
43	/-- Abstract allocation (§9 ¶1). Its identity is its key in `State.allocs`. `bytes` is
44	indexed by offset from `base`; offsets outside `[0, size)` are reached by no permitted
45	access (`Spatial`). `freeAuth = some d` records the deallocation token `d` of a
46	deallocatable allocation (§9 ¶1 b8, §17 ¶4); `none` marks a non-deallocatable one. -/
47	structure Alloc where
48	  space : Nat
49	  base : Nat
50	  size : Nat
51	  align : Nat
52	  live : Bool
53	  bytes : Nat → AByte
54	  freeAuth : Option Nat
55	
56	/-- Place of the minimal kernel: allocation identity, offset and length (§11 ¶1). -/
57	structure Place where
58	  alloc : Nat
59	  off : Nat
60	  len : Nat
61	
62	/-- Means of access: address, provenance (an allocation identity), length and elementary
63	access authority (§12 ¶1, §12 ¶2). -/
64	structure Access where
65	  addr : Nat
66	  prov : Nat
67	  len : Nat
68	  auth : Auth
69	
70	/-- Abstract state: registered allocations by identity, live or dead, and the counter `next`
71	representing the freshness discipline (§9 ¶7, §13 ¶1). -/
72	structure State where
73	  allocs : Nat → Option Alloc
74	  next : Nat
75	
76	/-- Well-formedness of identities and freshness: no identity at or above the counter is
77	registered (§9 ¶7, §9 ¶8 b1). -/
78	def WF (s : State) : Prop := ∀ i, s.next ≤ i → s.allocs i = none
79	
80	/-- Spatial containment of an access in an allocation (§15 ¶1; used by §15.2 and §16.2). -/
81	def Spatial (a : Alloc) (ac : Access) : Prop :=
82	  a.base ≤ ac.addr ∧ ac.addr + ac.len ≤ a.base + a.size
83	
84	/-- Spatial containment is decidable (§15 ¶1). -/
85	instance (a : Alloc) (ac : Access) : Decidable (Spatial a ac) :=
86	  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (a.base ≤ ac.addr ∧ ac.addr + ac.len ≤ a.base + a.size))
87	
88	/-- The `len` bytes from offset `off` are initialized (§15.3, read as: every byte of the
89	accessed range). -/
90	def Alloc.InitRange (a : Alloc) (off len : Nat) : Prop :=
91	  ∀ i, i < len → a.bytes (off + i) ≠ .uninit
92	
93	/-- Initialization of a range is decidable (§15.3). -/
94	instance (a : Alloc) (off len : Nat) : Decidable (a.InitRange off len) :=
95	  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ i, i < len → a.bytes (off + i) ≠ .uninit))
96	
97	/-- Kernel conditions of a raw typed read by `ac`: §15.1, §15.2, §15.3 and §15.5. The
98	conditions §15.4, §15.6 and §15.7 are the parametric obligations of `ReadOblSpec`. -/
99	def CanRead (s : State) (ac : Access) : Prop :=
100	  ∃ a, s.allocs ac.prov = some a ∧ a.live = true ∧ Spatial a ac ∧
101	    a.InitRange (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len ∧ Auth.read ≤ ac.auth
102	
103	/-- Kernel conditions of a raw typed write by `ac`: §16.1, §16.2 and §16.3. The conditions
104	§16.4–§16.6 are the parametric obligations of `WriteOblSpec`. -/
105	def CanWrite (s : State) (ac : Access) : Prop :=
106	  ∃ a, s.allocs ac.prov = some a ∧ a.live = true ∧ Spatial a ac ∧ Auth.write ≤ ac.auth
107	
108	/-- The kernel conditions of a read are decidable (§15). -/
109	instance (s : State) (ac : Access) : Decidable (CanRead s ac) :=
110	  match h : s.allocs ac.prov with
111	  | some a =>
112	    if hc : a.live = true ∧ Spatial a ac ∧ a.InitRange (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len ∧
113	        Auth.read ≤ ac.auth then isTrue ⟨a, h, hc⟩
114	    else isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, hb'⟩ => hc (by rw [h] at hb; cases hb; exact hb')
115	  | none => isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, _⟩ => by rw [h] at hb; cases hb
116	
117	/-- The kernel conditions of a write are decidable (§16). -/
118	instance (s : State) (ac : Access) : Decidable (CanWrite s ac) :=
119	  match h : s.allocs ac.prov with
120	  | some a =>
121	    if hc : a.live = true ∧ Spatial a ac ∧ Auth.write ≤ ac.auth then isTrue ⟨a, h, hc⟩
122	    else isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, hb'⟩ => hc (by rw [h] at hb; cases hb; exact hb')
123	  | none => isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, _⟩ => by rw [h] at hb; cases hb
124	
125	/-- Partial resolution of a means of access to a place (§11 ¶2): defined when the
126	provenance identifies a registered allocation, live or dead, that spatially contains the
127	access. It proves no right to read or write. -/
128	def Access.toPlace (s : State) (ac : Access) : Option Place :=
129	  match s.allocs ac.prov with
130	  | some a => if Spatial a ac then some ⟨ac.prov, ac.addr - a.base, ac.len⟩ else none
131	  | none => none
132	
133	/-- Characterization of resolution (§11 ¶2). -/
134	theorem toPlace_eq_some {s : State} {ac : Access} {p : Place} :
135	    ac.toPlace s = some p ↔
136	      ∃ a, s.allocs ac.prov = some a ∧ Spatial a ac ∧
137	        p = ⟨ac.prov, ac.addr - a.base, ac.len⟩ := by
138	  unfold Access.toPlace
139	  split
140	  · next a ha =>
141	    by_cases hs : Spatial a ac
142	    · simp [hs, ha, eq_comm]
143	    · simp [hs, ha]
144	  · next ha => simp [ha]
145	
146	/-- The `len` bytes of `a` from offset `off`: the value of a valid read (§20.2 ¶1). -/
147	def Alloc.bytesAt (a : Alloc) (off len : Nat) : List AByte :=
148	  (List.range len).map fun i => a.bytes (off + i)
149	
150	/-- The `len` written bytes from position `off` of the supplied representation `w`, each
151	initialized with its value and provenance (§16 ¶2, §16 ¶5). -/
152	def writtenBytes (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (off len : Nat) : List AByte :=
153	  (List.range len).map fun i => .init (w (off + i)).1 (w (off + i)).2
154	
155	/-- Effect of a valid write on storage (§16 ¶2, §10 ¶4): the bytes at offsets
156	`[off, off + len)` are replaced byte by byte by `w`, initialized with the supplied value and
157	provenance; other bytes are unchanged (§16 ¶3). -/
158	def Alloc.write (a : Alloc) (off len : Nat) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) : Alloc :=
159	  { a with bytes := fun j =>
160	      if off ≤ j ∧ j < off + len then .init (w (j - off)).1 (w (j - off)).2 else a.bytes j }
161	
162	/-- Effect of a valid write of `w` through `ac` on the state (§16 ¶2, §16 ¶3). -/
163	def State.write (s : State) (ac : Access) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) : State :=
164	  { s with allocs := fun i =>
165	      if i = ac.prov then (s.allocs i).map (fun a => a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w)
166	      else s.allocs i }
167	
168	/-- Conditions of a successful raw deallocation of `id` with presented authority `auth`
169	(§17.1, §17.2): live, deallocatable, and `auth` compatible with the recorded token under the
170	context relation `C` (§17 ¶2, §17 ¶4). -/
171	def CanDealloc (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (s : State) (id auth : Nat) : Prop :=
172	  ∃ a, s.allocs id = some a ∧ a.live = true ∧ ∃ d, a.freeAuth = some d ∧ C auth d
173	
174	/-- Deallocation conditions are decidable when compatibility is (§17, §20.3 ¶3). -/
175	instance {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} [DecidableRel C] (s : State) (id auth : Nat) :
176	    Decidable (CanDealloc C s id auth) :=
177	  match h : s.allocs id with
178	  | none => isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, _⟩ => by rw [h] at hb; cases hb
179	  | some a =>
180	    match hf : a.freeAuth with
181	    | none => isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, _, d, hd, _⟩ => by
182	        rw [h] at hb
183	        cases hb
184	        rw [hf] at hd
185	        cases hd
186	    | some d =>
187	      if hc : a.live = true ∧ C auth d then isTrue ⟨a, h, hc.1, d, hf, hc.2⟩
188	      else isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, hl, d', hd', hc'⟩ => hc (by
189	        rw [h] at hb
190	        cases hb
191	        rw [hf] at hd'
192	        cases hd'
193	        exact ⟨hl, hc'⟩)
194	
195	/-- Effect of a valid deallocation (§17 ¶3, §20.2 ¶2): `id` becomes dead and stays
196	registered (§13 ¶1). -/
197	def State.dealloc (s : State) (id : Nat) : State :=
198	  { s with allocs := fun i =>
199	      if i = id then (s.allocs i).map (fun a => { a with live := false }) else s.allocs i }
200	
201	/-- Effect of a valid raw creation (§9 ¶11, §13 ¶1, §20.2 ¶2): a live allocation under the
202	identity `s.next`, wholly uninitialized (§10 ¶5); the counter advances (§9 ¶7). -/
203	def State.alloc (s : State) (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat) : State :=
204	  { allocs := fun i =>
205	      if i = s.next then
206	        some { space, base, size, align, live := true, bytes := fun _ => .uninit, freeAuth }
207	      else s.allocs i
208	    next := s.next + 1 }
209	
210	/-- Half-open ranges `[b1, b1 + n1)` and `[b2, b2 + n2)` have an empty intersection (§9 ¶3). -/
211	def RangeDisjoint (b1 n1 b2 n2 : Nat) : Prop :=
212	  ∀ x, b1 ≤ x → x < b1 + n1 → b2 ≤ x → x < b2 + n2 → False
213	
214	/-- Arithmetic form of range disjointness (§9 ¶3). -/
215	theorem rangeDisjoint_iff {b1 n1 b2 n2 : Nat} :
216	    RangeDisjoint b1 n1 b2 n2 ↔ b1 + n1 ≤ b2 ∨ b2 + n2 ≤ b1 ∨ n1 = 0 ∨ n2 = 0 := by
217	  constructor
218	  · intro h
219	    rcases Nat.le_total b1 b2 with h12 | h12
220	    · by_cases hlt : b2 < b1 + n1
221	      · by_cases hn : 0 < n2
222	        · exact (h b2 h12 hlt (Nat.le_refl _) (by omega)).elim
223	        · omega
224	      · omega
225	    · by_cases hlt : b1 < b2 + n2
226	      · by_cases hn : 0 < n1
227	        · exact (h b1 (Nat.le_refl _) (by omega) h12 hlt).elim
228	        · omega
229	      · omega
230	  · intro h x h1 h2 h3 h4
231	    omega
232	
233	/-- Range disjointness is decidable (§9 ¶3). -/
234	instance (b1 n1 b2 n2 : Nat) : Decidable (RangeDisjoint b1 n1 b2 n2) :=
235	  decidable_of_iff _ rangeDisjoint_iff.symm
236	
237	/-- Disjointness of live allocations in the same address space (§9 ¶3, §9 ¶8 b2). -/
238	def LiveDisjoint (s : State) : Prop :=
239	  ∀ i j a b, i ≠ j → s.allocs i = some a → s.allocs j = some b →
240	    a.live = true → b.live = true → a.space = b.space →
241	    RangeDisjoint a.base a.size b.base b.size
242	
243	/-- `n` is a power of two (§9 ¶1 b5, §9 ¶4). -/
244	def Pow2 (n : Nat) : Prop := ∃ k, n = 2 ^ k
245	
246	/-- Bounded form of `Pow2` (§9 ¶4). -/
247	theorem pow2_iff (n : Nat) : Pow2 n ↔ ∃ k, k < n + 1 ∧ n = 2 ^ k :=
248	  ⟨fun ⟨k, hk⟩ => ⟨k, by have := @Nat.lt_two_pow_self k; omega, hk⟩, fun ⟨k, _, hk⟩ => ⟨k, hk⟩⟩
249	
250	/-- `Pow2` is decidable (§9 ¶4). -/
251	instance (n : Nat) : Decidable (Pow2 n) :=
252	  decidable_of_iff _ (pow2_iff n).symm
253	
254	/-- Operation preconditions of raw creation in space `space` (§9 ¶11): fresh identity
255	`s.next`, strictly positive power-of-two alignment, aligned base, no overlap with any live
256	allocation of the same space. -/
257	def AllocPre (s : State) (space base size align : Nat) : Prop :=
258	  s.allocs s.next = none ∧ 0 < align ∧ Pow2 align ∧ base % align = 0 ∧
259	    ∀ i a, s.allocs i = some a → a.live = true → a.space = space →
260	      RangeDisjoint a.base a.size base size
261	
262	/-- The entry `o` does not overlap `[base, base + size)` in space `space`: absent, dead, of
263	another space, or disjoint (§9 ¶11). -/
264	def NoOverlap (space base size : Nat) : Option Alloc → Prop
265	  | some a => a.live = true → a.space = space → RangeDisjoint a.base a.size base size
266	  | none => True
267	
268	/-- `NoOverlap` is decidable (§9 ¶11). -/
269	instance (space base size : Nat) : (o : Option Alloc) → Decidable (NoOverlap space base size o)
270	  | some a => inferInstanceAs
271	      (Decidable (a.live = true → a.space = space → RangeDisjoint a.base a.size base size))
272	  | none => inferInstanceAs (Decidable True)
273	
274	/-- Decidable form of `AllocPre`, checking overlap on identities below the counter only
275	(§9 ¶11, §20.3 ¶3). -/
276	def AllocPreDec (s : State) (space base size align : Nat) : Prop :=
277	  s.allocs s.next = none ∧ 0 < align ∧ Pow2 align ∧ base % align = 0 ∧
278	    ∀ i, i < s.next → NoOverlap space base size (s.allocs i)
279	
280	/-- `AllocPreDec` is decidable (§20.3 ¶3). -/
281	instance (s : State) (space base size align : Nat) :
282	    Decidable (AllocPreDec s space base size align) := by
283	  unfold AllocPreDec
284	  infer_instance
285	
286	/-- Under freshness, `AllocPreDec` is `AllocPre` (§9 ¶7, §9 ¶11). -/
287	theorem allocPreDec_iff {s : State} (hwf : WF s) {space base size align : Nat} :
288	    AllocPreDec s space base size align ↔ AllocPre s space base size align := by
289	  constructor
290	  · rintro ⟨hf, h0, h2, hm, hd⟩
291	    refine ⟨hf, h0, h2, hm, fun i a ha hl hsp => ?_⟩
292	    have hi : i < s.next := Nat.lt_of_not_le fun hle => by rw [hwf i hle] at ha; cases ha
293	    have := hd i hi
294	    rw [ha] at this
295	    exact this hl hsp
296	  · rintro ⟨hf, h0, h2, hm, hd⟩
297	    refine ⟨hf, h0, h2, hm, fun i _ => ?_⟩
298	    cases ha : s.allocs i with
299	    | none => trivial
300	    | some a => exact fun hl hsp => hd i a ha hl hsp
301	
302	/-- Alignment of every registered allocation, live or dead (§9 ¶4, §9 ¶8 b3). -/
303	def Aligned (s : State) : Prop :=
304	  ∀ i a, s.allocs i = some a → 0 < a.align ∧ Pow2 a.align ∧ a.base % a.align = 0
305	
306	/-- Admissible state (§9 ¶8): freshness, live disjointness, alignment. -/
307	structure Admissible (s : State) : Prop where
308	  wf : WF s
309	  disjoint : LiveDisjoint s
310	  aligned : Aligned s
311	
312	/-- The empty state: no allocation, counter `0` (§9 ¶9). -/
313	def State.empty : State := ⟨fun _ => none, 0⟩
314	
315	/-- The empty state is an admissible initial state (§9 ¶9). -/
316	theorem admissible_empty : Admissible State.empty :=
317	  ⟨fun _ _ => rfl, (fun _ _ _ _ _ h => nomatch h), (fun _ _ h => nomatch h)⟩
318	
319	/-! ## Restrictive derivation (§14) -/
320	
321	/-- `ac'` is a restrictive derivation of `ac` (§14 ¶1): same provenance, address subrange,
322	authority at most that of the source. -/
323	def Derive (ac ac' : Access) : Prop :=
324	  ac.addr ≤ ac'.addr ∧ ac'.addr + ac'.len ≤ ac.addr + ac.len ∧
325	    ac'.prov = ac.prov ∧ ac'.auth ≤ ac.auth
326	
327	/-- A restrictive derivation preserves provenance (§14 ¶1 b1). -/
328	theorem derive_prov {ac ac' : Access} (hd : Derive ac ac') : ac'.prov = ac.prov :=
329	  hd.2.2.1
330	
331	/-- A restrictive derivation of an access contained in an allocation is contained in it
332	(§14 ¶1 b2, §15 ¶1). -/
333	theorem derive_spatial {ac ac' : Access} (hd : Derive ac ac') {a : Alloc}
334	    (hs : Spatial a ac) : Spatial a ac' := by
335	  obtain ⟨h1, h2, -, -⟩ := hd
336	  obtain ⟨h3, h4⟩ := hs
337	  exact ⟨Nat.le_trans h3 h1, Nat.le_trans h2 h4⟩
338	
339	/-- A restrictive derivation confers no greater authority (§14 ¶1 b3). -/
340	theorem derive_auth_le {ac ac' : Access} (hd : Derive ac ac') : ac'.auth ≤ ac.auth :=
341	  hd.2.2.2
342	
343	/-! ## Parametric obligations and outcomes (§15 ¶5, §16 ¶4, §20) -/
344	
345	/-- Read obligations not defined by the kernel, §15.4, §15.6, §15.7 (§15 ¶5): explicit
346	predicates of the execution context (§20.3 ¶1), depending on the state, the access and the
347	read type; `dec` is the part with a decision procedure, `stat` the part established
348	statically or by contract (§20.3 ¶2). -/
349	structure ReadOblSpec (Ty : Type) where
350	  dec : State → Access → Ty → Prop
351	  stat : State → Access → Ty → Prop
352	
353	/-- Read obligations with a decision instance for `dec`, as required by a computable
354	interpreter (§20.3 ¶3). -/
355	structure ReadObl (Ty : Type) extends toSpec : ReadOblSpec Ty where
356	  decInst : ∀ s ac t, Decidable (dec s ac t)
357	
358	attribute [instance] ReadObl.decInst
359	
360	/-- Write obligations not defined by the kernel, §16.4, §16.5, §16.6 (§16 ¶4): explicit
361	predicates of the execution context (§20.3 ¶1), depending on the state, the access, the
362	written type and the supplied representation; split into `dec` and `stat` (§20.3 ¶2). -/
363	structure WriteOblSpec (Ty : Type) where
364	  dec : State → Access → Ty → (Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) → Prop
365	  stat : State → Access → Ty → (Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) → Prop
366	
367	/-- Write obligations with a decision instance for `dec`, as required by a computable
368	interpreter (§20.3 ¶3). -/
369	structure WriteObl (Ty : Type) extends toSpec : WriteOblSpec Ty where
370	  decInst : ∀ s ac t w, Decidable (dec s ac t w)
371	
372	attribute [instance] WriteObl.decInst
373	
374	/-- Outcome of a raw state-transforming operation: `ok` with the new state, or `ub`, which
375	supplies no state (§20.1 ¶2, §1). -/
376	inductive Outcome where
377	  | ok (s : State)
378	  | ub
379	
380	/-- Outcome of a raw read: `ok` with the bytes read, or `ub` (§20.1 ¶2, §20.2 ¶1). -/
381	inductive ReadOutcome where
382	  | ok (v : List AByte)
383	  | ub
384	  deriving DecidableEq
385	
386	section Relations
387	
388	variable {Ty : Type}
389	
390	/-- Raw typed read of type `t` through `ac` (§15, §20.1, §20.2 ¶1): `ok` with the bytes of
391	the accessed range when the kernel conditions (`CanRead`) and both parts of the obligations
392	hold; `ub` otherwise, a violated static part included (§20.1 ¶2 b2). The state is
393	unchanged. -/
394	inductive ReadStep (ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty) (ac : Access) (t : Ty) (s : State) :
395	    ReadOutcome → Prop where
396	  | ok {a : Alloc} : s.allocs ac.prov = some a → CanRead s ac ∧ ObR.dec s ac t ∧ ObR.stat s ac t →
397	      ReadStep ObR ac t s (.ok (a.bytesAt (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len))
398	  | ub : ¬ (CanRead s ac ∧ ObR.dec s ac t ∧ ObR.stat s ac t) → ReadStep ObR ac t s .ub
399	
400	/-- Raw typed write of `w` at type `t` through `ac` (§16, §20.1, §20.2 ¶2): `ok` with the
401	effect `State.write` when the kernel conditions (`CanWrite`) and both parts of the
402	obligations hold; `ub` otherwise (§20.1 ¶2 b2). -/
403	inductive WriteStep (ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty) (ac : Access) (t : Ty)
404	    (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (s : State) : Outcome → Prop where
405	  | ok : CanWrite s ac ∧ ObW.dec s ac t w ∧ ObW.stat s ac t w →
406	      WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok (s.write ac w))
407	  | ub : ¬ (CanWrite s ac ∧ ObW.dec s ac t w ∧ ObW.stat s ac t w) → WriteStep ObW ac t w s .ub
408	
409	end Relations
410	
411	/-- Raw deallocation of `id` with presented authority `auth` (§17, §20.1, §20.2 ¶2): `ok`
412	with the effect `State.dealloc` when `CanDealloc`; `ub` otherwise. `C` needs no decision
413	instance (§20.3 ¶3). -/
414	inductive DeallocStep (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (id auth : Nat) (s : State) : Outcome → Prop where
415	  | ok : CanDealloc C s id auth → DeallocStep C id auth s (.ok (s.dealloc id))
416	  | ub : ¬ CanDealloc C s id auth → DeallocStep C id auth s .ub
417	
418	/-- Raw creation (§9 ¶11, §20.1, §20.2 ¶2): `ok` with the effect `State.alloc` when
419	`AllocPre`; `ub` otherwise. -/
420	inductive AllocStep (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat) (s : State) :
421	    Outcome → Prop where
422	  | ok : AllocPre s space base size align →
423	      AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s (.ok (s.alloc space base size align freeAuth))
424	  | ub : ¬ AllocPre s space base size align → AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s .ub
425	
426	/-! ## Interpreters (§20.3 ¶3; `formal/DESIGN.md`, "Representation") -/
427	
428	section Interpreters
429	
430	variable {Ty : Type}
431	
432	/-- Interpreter of `ReadStep`: decides the kernel conditions and `dec`, takes the static
433	part `stat` as a proof argument (§20.3 ¶3), and returns the bytes read (§20.2 ¶1). -/
434	def read (ObR : ReadObl Ty) (ac : Access) (t : Ty) (s : State) (_hs : ObR.stat s ac t) :
435	    ReadOutcome :=
436	  match s.allocs ac.prov with
437	  | some a =>
438	    if CanRead s ac ∧ ObR.dec s ac t then .ok (a.bytesAt (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len) else .ub
439	  | none => .ub
440	
441	/-- Interpreter of `WriteStep`: decides the kernel conditions and `dec`, takes `stat` as a
442	proof argument (§20.3 ¶3). -/
443	def write (ObW : WriteObl Ty) (ac : Access) (t : Ty) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (s : State)
444	    (_hs : ObW.stat s ac t w) : Outcome :=
445	  if CanWrite s ac ∧ ObW.dec s ac t w then .ok (s.write ac w) else .ub
446	
447	end Interpreters
448	
449	/-- Interpreter of `DeallocStep`, given a decision instance for compatibility (§20.3 ¶3). -/
450	def dealloc (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) [DecidableRel C] (id auth : Nat) (s : State) : Outcome :=
451	  if CanDealloc C s id auth then .ok (s.dealloc id) else .ub
452	
453	/-- Interpreter of `AllocStep`, taking freshness `WF s` as a proof argument; it decides
454	`AllocPreDec`, which is `AllocPre` under `WF` (§9 ¶11, §20.3 ¶3). -/
455	def alloc (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat) (s : State) (_hwf : WF s) :
456	    Outcome :=
457	  if AllocPreDec s space base size align then .ok (s.alloc space base size align freeAuth)
458	  else .ub
459	
460	/-! ## Executions (§9 ¶9, §20.1 ¶2, §20.3 ¶3) -/
461	
462	/-- Raw operations of the machine (§15, §16, §17, §9 ¶11, §20.1). -/
463	inductive Op (Ty : Type) where
464	  | read (ac : Access) (t : Ty)
465	  | write (ac : Access) (t : Ty) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat)
466	  | dealloc (id auth : Nat)
467	  | alloc (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat)
468	
469	section Executions
470	
471	variable {Ty : Type}
472	
473	/-- `ok` transitions of the raw operations, with compatibility and obligations fixed by the
474	execution context (§20.1 ¶2, §20.3 ¶3). A read leaves the state unchanged (§20.2 ¶1). -/
475	inductive Step (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty) :
476	    Op Ty → State → State → Prop where
477	  | read {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {s : State} {v : List AByte} :
478	      ReadStep ObR ac t s (.ok v) → Step C ObR ObW (.read ac t) s s
479	  | write {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s s' : State} :
480	      WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok s') → Step C ObR ObW (.write ac t w) s s'
481	  | dealloc {id auth : Nat} {s s' : State} :
482	      DeallocStep C id auth s (.ok s') → Step C ObR ObW (.dealloc id auth) s s'
483	  | alloc {space base size align : Nat} {freeAuth : Option Nat} {s s' : State} :
484	      AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s (.ok s') →
485	      Step C ObR ObW (.alloc space base size align freeAuth) s s'
486	
487	/-- Execution: a sequence of `ok` steps under one context (§20.3 ¶3). A `ub` step supplies
488	no state, so it never occurs inside an execution (§20.1 ¶2 b3). -/
489	inductive Exec (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty) :
490	    List (Op Ty) → State → State → Prop where
491	  | nil (s : State) : Exec C ObR ObW [] s s
492	  | cons {op : Op Ty} {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s s' s'' : State} :
493	      Step C ObR ObW op s s' → Exec C ObR ObW ops s' s'' → Exec C ObR ObW (op :: ops) s s''
494	
495	/-- `s` is reachable from the initial state `s₀`, which need not be empty (§9 ¶9). -/
496	def Reachable (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty)
497	    (s₀ s : State) : Prop :=
498	  ∃ ops, Exec C ObR ObW ops s₀ s
499	
500	/-- The operation neither writes through provenance `i` nor deallocates `i`. Used to state
501	the "absence of an intervening write or invalidation" of §16 ¶5 for allocation `i`; writes
502	through other provenances are allowed (non-interference, §16 ¶5). -/
503	def Op.KeepsAlloc (i : Nat) : Op Ty → Prop
504	  | .read _ _ => True
505	  | .write ac _ _ => ac.prov ≠ i
506	  | .dealloc id _ => id ≠ i
507	  | .alloc .. => True
508	
509	end Executions
510	
511	/-! ## Outcome characterizations, determinism, totality (§20.1) -/
512	
513	section Theorems
514	
515	variable {Ty : Type}
516	
517	/-- `ok` outcome of a raw read (§15, §20.1 ¶2 b1, §20.2 ¶1). -/
518	theorem ReadStep_ok_iff {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {s : State}
519	    {v : List AByte} :
520	    ReadStep ObR ac t s (.ok v) ↔ (CanRead s ac ∧ ObR.dec s ac t ∧ ObR.stat s ac t) ∧
521	      ∃ a, s.allocs ac.prov = some a ∧ v = a.bytesAt (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len :=
522	  ⟨fun h => by cases h with | ok ha h => exact ⟨h, _, ha, rfl⟩,
523	   fun ⟨h, _, ha, e⟩ => by subst e; exact .ok ha h⟩
524	
525	/-- `ok` outcome of a raw write (§16, §20.1 ¶2 b1). -/
526	theorem WriteStep_ok_iff {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
527	    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s s' : State} :
528	    WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok s') ↔
529	      (CanWrite s ac ∧ ObW.dec s ac t w ∧ ObW.stat s ac t w) ∧ s' = s.write ac w :=
530	  ⟨fun h => by cases h with | ok h => exact ⟨h, rfl⟩, fun ⟨h, e⟩ => by subst e; exact .ok h⟩
531	
532	/-- `ok` outcome of a raw deallocation (§17, §20.1 ¶2 b1). -/
533	theorem DeallocStep_ok_iff {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {id auth : Nat} {s s' : State} :
534	    DeallocStep C id auth s (.ok s') ↔ CanDealloc C s id auth ∧ s' = s.dealloc id :=
535	  ⟨fun h => by cases h with | ok h => exact ⟨h, rfl⟩, fun ⟨h, e⟩ => by subst e; exact .ok h⟩
536	
537	/-- `ok` outcome of a raw creation (§9 ¶11, §20.1 ¶2 b1). -/
538	theorem AllocStep_ok_iff {space base size align : Nat} {freeAuth : Option Nat} {s s' : State} :
539	    AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s (.ok s') ↔
540	      AllocPre s space base size align ∧ s' = s.alloc space base size align freeAuth :=
541	  ⟨fun h => by cases h with | ok h => exact ⟨h, rfl⟩, fun ⟨h, e⟩ => by subst e; exact .ok h⟩
542	
543	/-- A raw read has at most one outcome (§20.1 ¶3). -/
544	theorem ReadStep_det {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {s : State}
545	    {o₁ o₂ : ReadOutcome} (h₁ : ReadStep ObR ac t s o₁) (h₂ : ReadStep ObR ac t s o₂) :
546	    o₁ = o₂ := by
547	  cases h₁ with
548	  | ok ha _ =>
549	    cases h₂ with
550	    | ok hb _ => rw [ha] at hb; cases hb; rfl
551	    | ub => contradiction
552	  | ub => cases h₂ with
553	    | ok => contradiction
554	    | ub => rfl
555	
556	/-- A raw write has at most one outcome (§20.1 ¶3). -/
557	theorem WriteStep_det {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
558	    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s : State} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome}
559	    (h₁ : WriteStep ObW ac t w s o₁) (h₂ : WriteStep ObW ac t w s o₂) : o₁ = o₂ := by
560	  cases h₁ <;> cases h₂ <;> first | rfl | contradiction
561	
562	/-- A raw deallocation has at most one outcome (§20.1 ¶3). -/
563	theorem DeallocStep_det {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {id auth : Nat} {s : State}
564	    {o₁ o₂ : Outcome} (h₁ : DeallocStep C id auth s o₁) (h₂ : DeallocStep C id auth s o₂) :
565	    o₁ = o₂ := by
566	  cases h₁ <;> cases h₂ <;> first | rfl | contradiction
567	
568	/-- A raw creation has at most one outcome (§20.1 ¶3). -/
569	theorem AllocStep_det {space base size align : Nat} {freeAuth : Option Nat} {s : State}
570	    {o₁ o₂ : Outcome} (h₁ : AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s o₁)
571	    (h₂ : AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s o₂) : o₁ = o₂ := by
572	  cases h₁ <;> cases h₂ <;> first | rfl | contradiction
573	
574	/-- Totality of the raw read on every state (§20.1 ¶3), in the constructive form
575	`¬¬∃`, classically equivalent to `∃`; `stat` has no decision procedure. -/
576	theorem ReadStep_total (ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty) (ac : Access) (t : Ty) (s : State) :
577	    ¬¬ ∃ o, ReadStep ObR ac t s o :=
578	  fun hn => hn ⟨.ub, .ub fun h => let ⟨_, ha, _⟩ := h.1; hn ⟨_, .ok ha h⟩⟩
579	
580	/-- Totality of the raw write on every state (§20.1 ¶3), constructive form `¬¬∃`. -/
581	theorem WriteStep_total (ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty) (ac : Access) (t : Ty)
582	    (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (s : State) : ¬¬ ∃ o, WriteStep ObW ac t w s o :=
583	  fun hn => hn ⟨.ub, .ub fun h => hn ⟨_, .ok h⟩⟩
584	
585	/-- Totality of the raw deallocation on every state (§20.1 ¶3), constructive form `¬¬∃`;
586	`C` has no decision procedure. -/
587	theorem DeallocStep_total (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (id auth : Nat) (s : State) :
588	    ¬¬ ∃ o, DeallocStep C id auth s o :=
589	  fun hn => hn ⟨.ub, .ub fun h => hn ⟨_, .ok h⟩⟩
590	
591	/-- Totality of the raw creation on every state (§20.1 ¶3), constructive form `¬¬∃`;
592	`AllocPre` quantifies over every identity. -/
593	theorem AllocStep_total (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat) (s : State) :
594	    ¬¬ ∃ o, AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s o :=
595	  fun hn => hn ⟨.ub, .ub fun h => hn ⟨_, .ok h⟩⟩
596	
597	/-! ## Agreement of the interpreters with the relations (§20.3 ¶3) -/
598	
599	/-- Soundness of `read`: its result is an outcome of `ReadStep` (§20.1, §20.3 ¶3). -/
600	theorem read_sound {ObR : ReadObl Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {s : State}
601	    {hs : ObR.stat s ac t} {o : ReadOutcome} (h : read ObR ac t s hs = o) :
602	    ReadStep ObR.toSpec ac t s o := by
603	  subst h
604	  unfold read
605	  split
606	  · next a ha =>
607	    split
608	    · next hc => exact .ok ha ⟨hc.1, hc.2, hs⟩
609	    · next hc => exact .ub fun ⟨h1, h2, _⟩ => hc ⟨h1, h2⟩
610	  · next ha => exact .ub fun ⟨⟨b, hb, _⟩, _⟩ => by rw [ha] at hb; cases hb
611	
612	/-- Completeness of `read`: every outcome of `ReadStep` is the result of `read`, for every
613	proof of the static part (§20.1, §20.3 ¶3). -/
614	theorem read_complete {ObR : ReadObl Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {s : State}
615	    {o : ReadOutcome} (h : ReadStep ObR.toSpec ac t s o) (hs : ObR.stat s ac t) :
616	    read ObR ac t s hs = o := by
617	  unfold read
618	  cases h with
619	  | ok ha hc =>
620	    split
621	    · next b hb =>
622	      rw [ha] at hb
623	      cases hb
624	      exact ite_eq_left ⟨hc.1, hc.2.1⟩
625	    · next hb => rw [ha] at hb; cases hb
626	  | ub hc =>
627	    split
628	    · exact ite_eq_right fun ⟨h1, h2⟩ => hc ⟨h1, h2, hs⟩
629	    · rfl
630	
631	/-- Soundness of `write` (§20.1, §20.3 ¶3). -/
632	theorem write_sound {ObW : WriteObl Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat}
633	    {s : State} {hs : ObW.stat s ac t w} {o : Outcome} (h : write ObW ac t w s hs = o) :
634	    WriteStep ObW.toSpec ac t w s o := by
635	  subst h
636	  unfold write
637	  split
638	  · next hc => exact .ok ⟨hc.1, hc.2, hs⟩
639	  · next hc => exact .ub fun ⟨h1, h2, _⟩ => hc ⟨h1, h2⟩
640	
641	/-- Completeness of `write`, for every proof of the static part (§20.1, §20.3 ¶3). -/
642	theorem write_complete {ObW : WriteObl Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
643	    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s : State} {o : Outcome}
644	    (h : WriteStep ObW.toSpec ac t w s o) (hs : ObW.stat s ac t w) :
645	    write ObW ac t w s hs = o := by
646	  unfold write
647	  cases h with
648	  | ok h => exact ite_eq_left ⟨h.1, h.2.1⟩
649	  | ub h => exact ite_eq_right fun ⟨h1, h2⟩ => h ⟨h1, h2, hs⟩
650	
651	end Theorems
652	
653	/-- Soundness of `dealloc` (§20.1, §20.3 ¶3). -/
654	theorem dealloc_sound {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} [DecidableRel C] {id auth : Nat} {s : State}
655	    {o : Outcome} (h : dealloc C id auth s = o) : DeallocStep C id auth s o := by
656	  subst h
657	  unfold dealloc
658	  split
659	  · next hc => exact .ok hc
660	  · next hc => exact .ub hc
661	
662	/-- Completeness of `dealloc` (§20.1, §20.3 ¶3). -/
663	theorem dealloc_complete {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} [DecidableRel C] {id auth : Nat} {s : State}
664	    {o : Outcome} (h : DeallocStep C id auth s o) : dealloc C id auth s = o := by
665	  unfold dealloc
666	  cases h with
667	  | ok h => exact ite_eq_left h
668	  | ub h => exact ite_eq_right h
669	
670	/-- Soundness of `alloc` on states satisfying `WF` (§9 ¶11, §20.1, §20.3 ¶3). -/
671	theorem alloc_sound {space base size align : Nat} {freeAuth : Option Nat} {s : State}
672	    {hwf : WF s} {o : Outcome} (h : alloc space base size align freeAuth s hwf = o) :
673	    AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s o := by
674	  subst h
675	  unfold alloc
676	  split
677	  · next hc => exact .ok ((allocPreDec_iff hwf).1 hc)
678	  · next hc => exact .ub (mt (allocPreDec_iff hwf).2 hc)
679	
680	/-- Completeness of `alloc`, for every proof of `WF` (§9 ¶11, §20.1, §20.3 ¶3). -/
681	theorem alloc_complete {space base size align : Nat} {freeAuth : Option Nat} {s : State}
682	    {o : Outcome} (h : AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s o) (hwf : WF s) :
683	    alloc space base size align freeAuth s hwf = o := by
684	  unfold alloc
685	  cases h with
686	  | ok h => exact ite_eq_left ((allocPreDec_iff hwf).2 h)
687	  | ub h => exact ite_eq_right (mt (allocPreDec_iff hwf).1 h)
688	
689	section Domain
690	
691	variable {Ty : Type}
692	
693	/-- On the interpreter's domain the raw read has an outcome, computed by `read` (§20.1 ¶3). -/
694	theorem ReadStep_total_on (ObR : ReadObl Ty) (ac : Access) (t : Ty) (s : State)
695	    (hs : ObR.stat s ac t) : ∃ o, ReadStep ObR.toSpec ac t s o :=
696	  ⟨_, read_sound (hs := hs) rfl⟩
697	
698	/-- On the interpreter's domain the raw write has an outcome, computed by `write`
699	(§20.1 ¶3). -/
700	theorem WriteStep_total_on (ObW : WriteObl Ty) (ac : Access) (t : Ty)
701	    (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (s : State) (hs : ObW.stat s ac t w) :
702	    ∃ o, WriteStep ObW.toSpec ac t w s o :=
703	  ⟨_, write_sound (hs := hs) rfl⟩
704	
705	end Domain
706	
707	/-- With decidable compatibility the raw deallocation has an outcome, computed by
708	`dealloc` (§20.1 ¶3). -/
709	theorem DeallocStep_total_on (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) [DecidableRel C] (id auth : Nat)
710	    (s : State) : ∃ o, DeallocStep C id auth s o :=
711	  ⟨_, dealloc_sound rfl⟩
712	
713	/-- On states satisfying `WF` the raw creation has an outcome, computed by `alloc`
714	(§20.1 ¶3). -/
715	theorem AllocStep_total_on (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat) (s : State)
716	    (hwf : WF s) : ∃ o, AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s o :=
717	  ⟨_, alloc_sound (hwf := hwf) rfl⟩
718	
719	/-! ## Effects: frame and invariants (§9, §13, §16 ¶2–¶3, §17 ¶3, §20.2 ¶2) -/
720	
721	/-- Entry of the written allocation after the write effect (§16 ¶2). -/
722	theorem State.write_allocs_self (s : State) (ac : Access) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) :
723	    (s.write ac w).allocs ac.prov =
724	      (s.allocs ac.prov).map (fun a => a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w) := by
725	  dsimp only [State.write]
726	  exact ite_eq_left rfl
727	
728	/-- Entry of the deallocated allocation after the deallocation effect (§17 ¶3). -/
729	theorem State.dealloc_allocs_self (s : State) (id : Nat) :
730	    (s.dealloc id).allocs id = (s.allocs id).map (fun a => { a with live := false }) := by
731	  dsimp only [State.dealloc]
732	  exact ite_eq_left rfl
733	
734	/-- Entry of the new allocation after the creation effect (§9 ¶11, §10 ¶5). -/
735	theorem State.alloc_allocs_self (s : State) (space base size align : Nat)
736	    (freeAuth : Option Nat) :
737	    (s.alloc space base size align freeAuth).allocs s.next =
738	      some { space, base, size, align, live := true, bytes := fun _ => .uninit, freeAuth } := by
739	  dsimp only [State.alloc]
740	  exact ite_eq_left rfl
741	
742	/-- Inside the written range, offset `off + i` holds the `i`-th written byte with its value
743	and provenance (§16 ¶2). -/
744	theorem Alloc.write_bytes_in (a : Alloc) {off len : Nat} (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat)
745	    {i : Nat} (hi : i < len) : (a.write off len w).bytes (off + i) = .init (w i).1 (w i).2 := by
746	  simp only [Alloc.write]
747	  rw [ite_eq_left ⟨Nat.le_add_right _ _, Nat.add_lt_add_left hi _⟩, Nat.add_sub_cancel_left]
748	
749	/-- Outside the written range, bytes are unchanged (§16 ¶3). -/
750	theorem Alloc.write_bytes_out (a : Alloc) {off len : Nat} (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat)
751	    {j : Nat} (hj : ¬ (off ≤ j ∧ j < off + len)) : (a.write off len w).bytes j = a.bytes j := by
752	  simp only [Alloc.write]
753	  exact ite_eq_right hj
754	
755	/-- Freshness is preserved by the write effect (§9 ¶7, §13 ¶3). -/
756	theorem write_wf {s : State} (hwf : WF s) (ac : Access) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) :
757	    WF (s.write ac w) := by
758	  intro i hi
759	  simp only [State.write, hwf i hi]
760	  split <;> rfl
761	
762	/-- Freshness is preserved by the deallocation effect (§9 ¶7, §13 ¶3). -/
763	theorem dealloc_wf {s : State} (hwf : WF s) (id : Nat) : WF (s.dealloc id) := by
764	  intro i hi
765	  simp only [State.dealloc, hwf i hi]
766	  split <;> rfl
767	
768	/-- Freshness is preserved by the creation effect (§9 ¶7, §13 ¶1). -/
769	theorem alloc_wf {s : State} (hwf : WF s) (space base size align : Nat)
770	    (freeAuth : Option Nat) : WF (s.alloc space base size align freeAuth) := by
771	  intro i hi
772	  have hi' : s.next + 1 ≤ i := hi
773	  have hne : i ≠ s.next := fun e => by rw [e] at hi'; exact Nat.not_succ_le_self _ hi'
774	  simp only [State.alloc]
775	  rw [ite_eq_right hne]
776	  exact hwf i (Nat.le_of_succ_le hi')
777	
778	/-- A step that makes no allocation live and keeps space, base and extent of every
779	allocation that stays live preserves live disjointness (§9 ¶3). -/
780	theorem LiveDisjoint.of_fields {s s' : State} (hd : LiveDisjoint s)
781	    (h : ∀ i a, s'.allocs i = some a → a.live = true →
782	      ∃ a₀, s.allocs i = some a₀ ∧ a₀.live = true ∧ a₀.space = a.space ∧
783	        a₀.base = a.base ∧ a₀.size = a.size) :
784	    LiveDisjoint s' := by
785	  intro i j a b hij ha hb hla hlb hsp
786	  obtain ⟨a₀, ha₀, hla₀, hs₁, hb₁, hz₁⟩ := h i a ha hla
787	  obtain ⟨b₀, hb₀, hlb₀, hs₂, hb₂, hz₂⟩ := h j b hb hlb
788	  have := hd i j a₀ b₀ hij ha₀ hb₀ hla₀ hlb₀ (by rw [hs₁, hs₂, hsp])
789	  rw [hb₁, hz₁, hb₂, hz₂] at this
790	  exact this

794	    (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) : LiveDisjoint (s.write ac w) :=
795	  hd.of_fields fun i a ha hla => by
796	    simp only [State.write] at ha
797	    split at ha
798	    · obtain ⟨a₀, h₀, rfl⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 ha
799	      exact ⟨a₀, h₀, hla, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
800	    · exact ⟨a, ha, hla, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

803	theorem liveDisjoint_dealloc {s : State} (hd : LiveDisjoint s) (id : Nat) :
804	    LiveDisjoint (s.dealloc id) :=
805	  hd.of_fields fun i a ha hla => by
806	    simp only [State.dealloc] at ha
807	    split at ha
808	    · obtain ⟨a₀, -, rfl⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 ha
809	      exact nomatch hla
810	    · exact ⟨a, ha, hla, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

813	§9 ¶11). -/
814	theorem liveDisjoint_alloc {s : State} (hd : LiveDisjoint s) {space base size align : Nat}
815	    (hp : AllocPre s space base size align) (freeAuth : Option Nat) :
816	    LiveDisjoint (s.alloc space base size align freeAuth) := by
817	  obtain ⟨-, -, -, -, hdis⟩ := hp
818	  intro i j a b hij ha hb hla hlb hsp
819	  simp only [State.alloc] at ha hb
820	  by_cases hi : i = s.next <;> by_cases hj : j = s.next
821	  · exact absurd (hi.trans hj.symm) hij
822	  · rw [ite_eq_left hi] at ha
823	    rw [ite_eq_right hj] at hb
824	    cases ha
825	    exact fun x h1 h2 h3 h4 => hdis j b hb hlb hsp.symm x h3 h4 h1 h2
826	  · rw [ite_eq_right hi] at ha
827	    rw [ite_eq_left hj] at hb
828	    cases hb
829	    exact hdis i a ha hla hsp
830	  · rw [ite_eq_right hi] at ha
831	    rw [ite_eq_right hj] at hb
832	    exact hd i j a b hij ha hb hla hlb hsp

835	theorem aligned_write {s : State} (h : Aligned s) (ac : Access) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) :
836	    Aligned (s.write ac w) := by
837	  intro i a ha
838	  simp only [State.write] at ha
839	  split at ha
840	  · obtain ⟨a₀, h₀, rfl⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 ha
841	    exact h i a₀ h₀
842	  · exact h i a ha

844	/-- Alignment is preserved by the deallocation effect (§9 ¶4). -/
845	theorem aligned_dealloc {s : State} (h : Aligned s) (id : Nat) : Aligned (s.dealloc id) := by
846	  intro i a ha
847	  simp only [State.dealloc] at ha
848	  split at ha
849	  · obtain ⟨a₀, h₀, rfl⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 ha
850	    exact h i a₀ h₀
851	  · exact h i a ha

854	theorem aligned_alloc {s : State} (h : Aligned s) {space base size align : Nat}

866

869	/-- An `ok` raw write preserves admissibility (§9 ¶8, §20.2 ¶2). -/
870	theorem WriteStep_admissible {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
871	    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s s' : State} (h : WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok s'))
872	    (hs : Admissible s) : Admissible s' := by
873	  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := WriteStep_ok_iff.1 h
874	  exact ⟨write_wf hs.wf ac w, liveDisjoint_write hs.disjoint ac w, aligned_write hs.aligned ac w⟩
875	
876	/-- An `ok` raw deallocation preserves admissibility (§9 ¶8, §20.2 ¶2). -/
877	theorem DeallocStep_admissible {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {id auth : Nat} {s s' : State}
878	    (h : DeallocStep C id auth s (.ok s')) (hs : Admissible s) : Admissible s' := by
879	  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := DeallocStep_ok_iff.1 h
880	  exact ⟨dealloc_wf hs.wf id, liveDisjoint_dealloc hs.disjoint id,
881	    aligned_dealloc hs.aligned id⟩

883	/-- An `ok` raw creation preserves admissibility (§9 ¶8, §9 ¶11, §20.2 ¶2). -/
884	theorem AllocStep_admissible {space base size align : Nat} {freeAuth : Option Nat}
885	    {s s' : State} (h : AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s (.ok s'))
886	    (hs : Admissible s) : Admissible s' := by
887	  obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := AllocStep_ok_iff.1 h
888	  exact ⟨alloc_wf hs.wf space base size align freeAuth, liveDisjoint_alloc hs.disjoint hp freeAuth,
889	    aligned_alloc hs.aligned hp freeAuth⟩

891	/-- Every `ok` step preserves admissibility (§9 ¶8, §20.2 ¶2). -/
892	theorem Step.admissible {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
893	    {op : Op Ty} {s s' : State} (h : Step C ObR ObW op s s') (hs : Admissible s) :
894	    Admissible s' := by
895	  cases h with
896	  | read _ => exact hs
897	  | write h => exact WriteStep_admissible h hs
898	  | dealloc h => exact DeallocStep_admissible h hs
899	  | alloc h => exact AllocStep_admissible h hs

901	/-- Every state of an execution from an admissible initial state is admissible
902	(§9 ¶8, §9 ¶9). -/
903	theorem Exec.admissible {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
904	    {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s₀ s : State} (h : Exec C ObR ObW ops s₀ s) (h₀ : Admissible s₀) :
905	    Admissible s := by
906	  induction h with
907	  | nil => exact h₀
908	  | cons hs _ ih => exact ih (hs.admissible h₀)

911	theorem Reachable.admissible {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty}
912	    {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {s₀ s : State} (h : Reachable C ObR ObW s₀ s)
913	    (h₀ : Admissible s₀) : Admissible s :=
914	  let ⟨_, he⟩ := h
915	  he.admissible h₀

917	/-- Frame of an `ok` raw write (§16 ¶3, §13 ¶3): other allocations unchanged; in the target
918	only bytes change, and only inside the written range; the counter is unchanged. -/
919	theorem WriteStep_frame {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
920	    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s s' : State} (h : WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok s')) :
921	    (∀ i, i ≠ ac.prov → s'.allocs i = s.allocs i) ∧
922	    (∃ a a', s.allocs ac.prov = some a ∧ s'.allocs ac.prov = some a' ∧
923	      { a' with bytes := a.bytes } = a ∧
924	      ∀ j, ¬ (ac.addr - a.base ≤ j ∧ j < ac.addr - a.base + ac.len) → a'.bytes j = a.bytes j) ∧
925	    s'.next = s.next := by
926	  obtain ⟨⟨⟨a, ha, -⟩, -⟩, rfl⟩ := WriteStep_ok_iff.1 h
927	  refine ⟨fun i hi => by simp only [State.write]; exact ite_eq_right hi,
928	    ⟨a, a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w, ha, ?_, rfl,
929	      fun j hj => Alloc.write_bytes_out a w hj⟩, rfl⟩
930	  rw [State.write_allocs_self, ha]
931	  rfl

933	/-- Frame of an `ok` raw deallocation (§17 ¶3, §13): other allocations unchanged; the target
934	only becomes dead and stays registered; the counter is unchanged. -/
935	theorem DeallocStep_frame {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {id auth : Nat} {s s' : State}
936	    (h : DeallocStep C id auth s (.ok s')) :
937	    (∀ i, i ≠ id → s'.allocs i = s.allocs i) ∧
938	    (∃ a, s.allocs id = some a ∧ s'.allocs id = some { a with live := false }) ∧
939	    s'.next = s.next := by
940	  obtain ⟨⟨a, ha, -⟩, rfl⟩ := DeallocStep_ok_iff.1 h
941	  refine ⟨fun i hi => by simp only [State.dealloc]; exact ite_eq_right hi, ⟨a, ha, ?_⟩, rfl⟩
942	  rw [State.dealloc_allocs_self, ha]
943	  rfl

945	/-- Frame of an `ok` raw creation (§13 ¶3, §9 ¶11, §10 ¶5): the identity `s.next` was
946	unregistered, every other entry is unchanged, the new allocation is live and wholly
947	uninitialized, and the counter advances. -/
948	theorem AllocStep_frame {space base size align : Nat} {freeAuth : Option Nat} {s s' : State}
949	    (h : AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s (.ok s')) :
950	    s.allocs s.next = none ∧ (∀ i, i ≠ s.next → s'.allocs i = s.allocs i) ∧
951	    s'.allocs s.next =
952	      some { space, base, size, align, live := true, bytes := fun _ => .uninit, freeAuth } ∧
953	    s'.next = s.next + 1 := by
954	  obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := AllocStep_ok_iff.1 h
955	  exact ⟨hp.1, fun i hi => by simp only [State.alloc]; exact ite_eq_right hi,
956	    State.alloc_allocs_self s space base size align freeAuth, rfl⟩

958	/-! ## Liveness, invalidation, identities across executions (§13, §15.1, §16.1, §17) -/

960	/-- An `ok` raw read resolves to a live allocation (§15.1). -/
961	theorem read_requires_live {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {s : State}
962	    {v : List AByte} (h : ReadStep ObR ac t s (.ok v)) :
963	    ∃ a, s.allocs ac.prov = some a ∧ a.live = true :=
964	  let ⟨⟨⟨a, ha, hl, _⟩, _⟩, _⟩ := ReadStep_ok_iff.1 h
965	  ⟨a, ha, hl⟩
966	
967	/-- An `ok` raw write resolves to a live allocation (§16.1). -/
968	theorem write_requires_live {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
969	    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s s' : State} (h : WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok s')) :
970	    ∃ a, s.allocs ac.prov = some a ∧ a.live = true :=
971	  let ⟨⟨⟨a, ha, hl, _⟩, _⟩, _⟩ := WriteStep_ok_iff.1 h
972	  ⟨a, ha, hl⟩

974	/-- A raw read through the provenance of a dead allocation is `ub` (§15.1, §17 ¶3). -/
975	theorem ReadStep_dead {R : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {s : State} {a : Alloc}
976	    {o : ReadOutcome} (ha : s.allocs ac.prov = some a) (hd : a.live = false)
977	    (h : ReadStep R ac t s o) : o = .ub := by
978	  cases h with
979	  | ok _ hc =>
980	    obtain ⟨b, hb, hl, _⟩ := hc.1
981	    rw [ha] at hb
982	    cases hb
983	    rw [hd] at hl
984	    exact nomatch hl
985	  | ub => rfl
986	
987	/-- A raw write through the provenance of a dead allocation is `ub` (§16.1, §17 ¶3). -/
988	theorem WriteStep_dead {W : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
989	    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s : State} {a : Alloc} {o : Outcome}
990	    (ha : s.allocs ac.prov = some a) (hd : a.live = false) (h : WriteStep W ac t w s o) :
991	    o = .ub := by
992	  cases h with
993	  | ok hc =>
994	    obtain ⟨b, hb, hl, _⟩ := hc.1
995	    rw [ha] at hb
996	    cases hb
997	    rw [hd] at hl
998	    exact nomatch hl
999	  | ub => rfl

1001	/-- A raw deallocation of a dead allocation is `ub` (§17.1, §17 ¶3). -/
1002	theorem DeallocStep_dead {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {id auth : Nat} {s : State} {a : Alloc}
1003	    {o : Outcome} (ha : s.allocs id = some a) (hd : a.live = false)
1004	    (h : DeallocStep C id auth s o) : o = .ub := by
1005	  cases h with
1006	  | ok hc =>
1007	    obtain ⟨b, hb, hl, _⟩ := hc
1008	    rw [ha] at hb
1009	    cases hb
1010	    rw [hd] at hl
1011	    exact nomatch hl
1012	  | ub => rfl

1014	/-- An `ok` step that neither writes through `i` nor deallocates `i` leaves the registered
1015	entry `i` unchanged (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3, §17 ¶3). -/
1016	theorem Step.keeps {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
1017	    {op : Op Ty} {s s' : State} (h : Step C ObR ObW op s s') {i : Nat} {a : Alloc}
1018	    (hk : op.KeepsAlloc i) (ha : s.allocs i = some a) : s'.allocs i = some a := by
1019	  cases h with
1020	  | read _ => exact ha
1021	  | @write ac _ w _ _ hw =>
1022	    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := WriteStep_ok_iff.1 hw
1023	    have hk : ac.prov ≠ i := hk
1024	    simp only [State.write]
1025	    rw [ite_eq_right (Ne.symm hk)]
1026	    exact ha
1027	  | @dealloc id _ _ _ hd =>
1028	    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := DeallocStep_ok_iff.1 hd
1029	    have hk : id ≠ i := hk
1030	    simp only [State.dealloc]
1031	    rw [ite_eq_right (Ne.symm hk)]
1032	    exact ha
1033	  | alloc hal =>
1034	    obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := AllocStep_ok_iff.1 hal
1035	    have hne : i ≠ s.next := fun e => by rw [e, hp.1] at ha; cases ha
1036	    simp only [State.alloc]
1037	    rw [ite_eq_right hne]
1038	    exact ha

1040	/-- No `ok` step writes through or deallocates a dead allocation (§16.1, §17.1). -/
1041	theorem Step.keepsAlloc_of_dead {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty}
1042	    {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {op : Op Ty} {s s' : State} (h : Step C ObR ObW op s s') {i : Nat}
1043	    {a : Alloc} (ha : s.allocs i = some a) (hd : a.live = false) : op.KeepsAlloc i := by
1044	  cases h with
1045	  | read _ => trivial
1046	  | @write ac _ _ _ _ hw =>
1047	    show ac.prov ≠ i
1048	    intro e
1049	    rw [← e] at ha
1050	    exact nomatch WriteStep_dead ha hd hw
1051	  | @dealloc id _ _ _ hdl =>
1052	    show id ≠ i
1053	    intro e
1054	    rw [← e] at ha
1055	    exact nomatch DeallocStep_dead ha hd hdl
1056	  | alloc _ => trivial

1058	/-- An `ok` step keeps every registered identity registered (§13 ¶1). -/
1059	theorem Step.registered {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
1060	    {op : Op Ty} {s s' : State} (h : Step C ObR ObW op s s') {i : Nat} {a : Alloc}
1061	    (ha : s.allocs i = some a) : ∃ a', s'.allocs i = some a' := by
1062	  cases h with
1063	  | read _ => exact ⟨a, ha⟩
1064	  | @write ac _ w _ _ hw =>
1065	    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := WriteStep_ok_iff.1 hw
1066	    simp only [State.write]
1067	    split
1068	    · exact ⟨_, by rw [ha]; rfl⟩
1069	    · exact ⟨a, ha⟩
1070	  | @dealloc id _ _ _ hd =>
1071	    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := DeallocStep_ok_iff.1 hd
1072	    simp only [State.dealloc]
1073	    split
1074	    · exact ⟨_, by rw [ha]; rfl⟩
1075	    · exact ⟨a, ha⟩
1076	  | alloc hal => exact ⟨a, (Step.alloc (C := C) (ObR := ObR) (ObW := ObW) hal).keeps trivial ha⟩
1077	
1078	/-- Along an execution whose operations neither write through `i` nor deallocate `i`, the
1079	registered entry `i` is unchanged (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3, §16 ¶5). -/
1080	theorem Exec.keeps {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
1081	    {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s s' : State} (h : Exec C ObR ObW ops s s') {i : Nat} {a : Alloc}
1082	    (hk : ∀ op ∈ ops, op.KeepsAlloc i) (ha : s.allocs i = some a) : s'.allocs i = some a := by
1083	  induction h with
1084	  | nil => exact ha
1085	  | cons hs _ ih =>
1086	    exact ih (fun op hop => hk op (List.Mem.tail _ hop)) (hs.keeps (hk _ (List.Mem.head _)) ha)
1087	
1088	/-- A dead allocation stays registered and dead, unchanged, in every later state of an
1089	execution (§13 ¶1). -/
1090	theorem dead_persists {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
1091	    {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s s' : State} (h : Exec C ObR ObW ops s s') {i : Nat} {a : Alloc}
1092	    (ha : s.allocs i = some a) (hd : a.live = false) : s'.allocs i = some a := by
1093	  induction h with
1094	  | nil => exact ha
1095	  | cons hs _ ih => exact ih (hs.keeps (hs.keepsAlloc_of_dead ha hd) ha)

1098	(§13 ¶1). -/
1099	theorem Exec.registered {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
1100	    {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s s' : State} (h : Exec C ObR ObW ops s s') {i : Nat} {a : Alloc}
1101	    (ha : s.allocs i = some a) : ∃ a', s'.allocs i = some a' := by
1102	  induction h generalizing a with
1103	  | nil => exact ⟨a, ha⟩
1104	  | cons hs _ ih =>
1105	    obtain ⟨a', ha'⟩ := hs.registered ha
1106	    exact ih ha'

1108	/-- An identity registered at some point of an execution is never assigned again by a later
1109	creation (§13 ¶1). -/
1110	theorem alloc_identity_never_reused {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty}
1111	    {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s s' s'' : State}
1112	    (h : Exec C ObR ObW ops s s') {i : Nat} {a : Alloc} (ha : s.allocs i = some a)
1113	    {space base size align : Nat} {freeAuth : Option Nat}
1114	    (hal : AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s' (.ok s'')) : i ≠ s'.next := by
1115	  intro e
1116	  obtain ⟨a', ha'⟩ := h.registered ha
1117	  rw [e, (AllocStep_frame hal).1] at ha'
1118	  cases ha'

1120	/-- After an `ok` raw deallocation of `i`, in every later state of an execution, every
1121	raw read and every raw write through provenance `i` is `ub` (§17 ¶3, §13 ¶2). -/
1122	theorem dealloc_invalidates {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty}
1123	    {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {i auth : Nat} {s s₁ s₂ : State} {ops : List (Op Ty)}
1124	    (hd : DeallocStep C i auth s (.ok s₁)) (he : Exec C ObR ObW ops s₁ s₂) {ac : Access}
1125	    (hp : ac.prov = i) :
1126	    (∀ (R : ReadOblSpec Ty) (t : Ty) (o : ReadOutcome), ReadStep R ac t s₂ o → o = .ub) ∧
